reviews.text: I’ve been taking my dog there for a little over a year and I’ve had an excellent experience with daycare and training and boarding on every visit. Giant shout out to the sweet staff on commerce Street and special thanks to Caitlin for her expertise.
I cannot say right now.
My experience with "Sit Means Sit" has been great so far! My little guy has learned so much.

The staff was very friendly and helpful, but I’m disappointed with how the group classes are handled. I signed up for the Silver training program, which includes 25 group credits, and I’ve already completed all of my private training. However, it has been a hassle just to begin using those credits because a group class won’t be held unless at least four people sign up. We all paid for group classes, so repeatedly postponing them makes it difficult to use what we purchased. At this rate, it could take years—possibly six—to use all 25 credits.

Better alternatives would be to hold scheduled classes even with fewer than four participants, offer semi-private sessions when enrollment is low, allow unused group credits to be converted to private training or other services, or provide an extension or refund when classes aren’t available. A reliable recurring schedule, waitlist, and additional classes based on demand would make the program much more usable.
My puppy had his first day today! Everything went great and I enjoyed getting an update with photos throughout the day! He looked so happy

I couldn't be happier with the care Louie receives at this facility! From the moment we arrive, he's excited and eager to go in, which gives me tremendous peace of mind knowing he's happy and comfortable there. The staff genuinely care about the dogs and provide outstanding attention and care every visit.
One of my favorite things is the daily updates, complete with pictures, that let me see how much fun Louie is having throughout the day. The communication is excellent, and it's clear that they take the time to get to know each dog's personality and needs.
Louie always comes home happy, tired, and well cared for. I highly recommend this facility to anyone looking for a safe, professional, and loving environment for their dog!

Love this place perfect for my dog she seems like she’s having the time of her life. Love the check in pictures and updates 💕definitely going back

From the start the team at Sit Means Sit has been wonderful. I am so glad I found them for my pup. During intake, the staff member took time and sat with me to explain the entire training process, which is pretty comprehensive and to meet our pup before ever committing to anything. You can tell everyone here enjoys what they do. I found the pricing to to be reasonable for everything that’s included. Communication is great with the staff. The option for applying credits toward daycare is also fantastic, so nice to get updates like the one I’m sharing. Our trainer was Clarissa. She is excellent, so thorough and very knowledgeable. She knows her stuff and really helped us LEARN how train our dog. Our pup listens to commands so much better now and more consistently even without the use of the E collar. And the group classes are really engaging for the pups. Can’t really get that kind of training otherwise. I would hands down recommend SMS Dallas 10/10.
They are good to the dogs. The staff truly cares for them.

He’s extremely stubborn and he’s only about 10 months old, so I didn’t expect him to be “perfect” when I came back from  a week’s vacation but I can definitely see the improvements!! It’s much easier to walk him now!!  I love the photos & updates I received every day. And I appreciate the one on one personal training with Caitlin today when picking up Romo. This will build confidence for both Romo and me!!l I am grateful for this service!! Thank you!! 🐾

June 2026
ROMO 👋🏽 and his parents truly appreciate the service we get here at Sit Means Sit.
We feel at ease when he’s here.
Thank You!!

Our dog is dropped off for boarding and daycare with his tail wagging and a smile on his face, we couldn’t ask for better peace of mind!!

We just sent our 5 month old golden retriever puppy, Barley, for a 2-week board and train program with Sit Means Sit, and I cannot rave more about the experience!

First of all, the team was amazing to work with. From my first inquiry call, I could tell they were different. They were thorough in explaining their training process, tools, philosophy, and more. They updated Barleys portal daily with photos, videos, and pupdates. They also worked with us on a payment plan that worked for us all and were able to get Barley in on a short notice.

The training Barley received has left my husband and I stunned. Barley has come home with obedience that will last a lifetime. He is an amazing walker (something that felt impossible before), he is great with heel, leave it, place, stay, and so much more. Barley has always been a good boy, but he really struggled with impulse control, and we couldn't imagine him getting to this point.

Above all else, training has given Barley a new set of confidence. He is still his sweet, goofy, puppy self, but he is so much more assured of himself and his surroundings. We are so grateful, thanks Sit Means Sit team!
I tried other trainers prior to coming to Sit Means Sit and finally found the answer for our pup! They’ve been great and he’s so happy and well behaved after only going through half of the program.
It was great. This was my dog's first time going to the daycare and she loved it when I picked her up, got her home, she was so exhausted, she's slept for the rest of the day.

It was Ash's first time at a boarding facility and he seemed to love it at SMS. He is a high energy anxious pup so I was a bit nervous to leave him, but the trainers and the staff said he was very comfortable and was getting lots of exercise. Overall, I am really happy with our first boarding experience and would recommend this facility!

My new puppy is loving his experience at Sit Means Sit Dallas. He is in puppy boot camp and is learning so much as also in daycare from time to time. His confidence is a remarkable improvement. And, the trainers and staff are loving and treat him so well. Could not be happier with the service!

I have been using Sit Means Sit Dallas for two years for both dog training and boarding my dog-reactive dog. Initially, I was skeptical, as I had never boarded a dog prior, and have had more than 10 years of successful at-home training dogs that were re-homed for reactivity, bite records, or or poor home matches. However, my most recent dog needed additional intervention due to severe dog-reactivity and several a prior re-home. Enter SMS. We did a 19 day board and train, and have been going to them since for boarding and weekly classes. They are life changers.

My dog absolutely LOVES boarding, and weekly classes (as evidenced by his screams of joy on the way to the facility, and his greeting by name to many pets and scratches). They have the utmost professionalism and flexibility with allowing us to board on short notice due to my constantly-moving work schedule, and their training regarding dog reactivity has allowed us to move in the community with more confidence. Finally, we have come to be a part of a community of dogs in training, and we have come a long way. 10/10 would recommend.

We were very nervous about doing training and leaving our dog for a couple of weeks, but they were very comforting and answered all our questions! They sent us updates and pictures everyday and took such good care of our pup. They helped us out so much and continue to do so!

A Lifesaver for Our Family and Our Dog

Our 8-year-old German Shepherd mix, Justice, has had a rough start in life. She’s fiercely loyal, but anxiety and a protective streak can make her reactive toward strangers—especially in our home. Finding a place where she could be safe, understood, and genuinely cared for felt impossible... until we found Sit Means Sit.

This isn't just another dog training and boarding facility. The staff here truly sees the dog behind the behaviors. They welcomed Justice with open arms, despite her history of aggression, and have always treated her like family. It’s hard to express how much that means to us. They remember her quirks, respect her boundaries, and—most importantly—shower her with affection, belly rubs, and a sense of calm she doesn’t always get elsewhere.

A couple years ago, they played a key role in her training, and ever since, they’ve continued to support her progress whenever she boards. Knowing she’s in an environment where she’s not just tolerated but truly loved gives us so much peace of mind.

Sit Means Sit gave Justice a chance to be herself—and gave us a break from worrying. We’ll always be grateful for that.

I adopted my dog, Turtle, a while back when suddenly he started showing signs of reactivity towards dogs. He did not listen to simple commands and was unruly. I had a consultation at Sit Means Sit and knew I wanted to work with them ASAP. Training is worth every penny, but it is expensive. That’s why I am so grateful SMS allowed me to utilize a payment plan that fit my budget in order to get my dog the training we desperately needed. It only took 2 sessions to see a difference in Turtle’s obedience and understanding. We had private sessions then I practiced with him at home for about 10-15 mins per day until our next session so that we were able to work on more challenging commands. Turtle and I are much happier now. I also use SMS for boarding and when I pick Turtle up, his behavior and temperament is always better than when I dropped him off. I can’t recommend SMS and our trainer Abby enough. We can walk and even go to the dog park without having to worry about reactivity. Thank you guys so much!

I was looking into this place and the reviews looked great, but when I spoke to a friend who trains dogs to become service dogs for blind people, she said that their trainers often use shock collars and pinching collars as methods. This can actually make the dogs worst, but in top of that it can traumatize them. So glad she told me this before I moved forward with them.

She says she thinks it does depend on the trainer, so just make sure the training methods are clear when you talk to specific trainers they have. My friend did say sometimes places will downplay or lie about their methods of training so just beware.
